Hon'ble Rajiv Gupta,J.
1.

Sri C.P. Tripathi, Advocate has filed counter affidavit alongwith the vakalatnama on behalf of the
opposite party No. 2 today in Court, which is taken on record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State, Shri C.P. Tripathi, learned counsel for the opposite party No. 2 and perused the record.

3. This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed with a prayer to quash the charge sheet dated 7.7.2022 and cognizance/summoning order dated 5.4.2023 as well as entire proceedings of Criminal Case No. 39 of 2023 (State vs. Devesh Garg) arising out of Case Crime No. 15 of 2022,

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that opposite party No. 2 is the wife of applicant No. 1.

Applicant No. 2 and 3 are the brothers in-law of opposite party No. 2 whereas applicant No. 4 is the mama and applicant Nos. 5 and 6 are the mother in-law and father in-law opposite party No.
2.

Learned counsel for the applicant has next submitted that on account of matrimonial discord, the present criminal case was instituted against the applicants, however, with the intervention of the respected members of both the family and society, they have amicably settled all their disputes and differences and now they do not have any grievance against the each other.

5. Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that a settlement-agreement dated 27.5.2023 has been drawn between the parties, a copy of which has been annexed as Annexue No. 4 to this application.

6. Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that applicant No. 1 and opposite party No.
2 have restored their relationship and are living together as husband and wife for the last 4-5 months and leading a happy married life.
7. Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that in view of the compromise made between the parties, the entire proceedings be quashed.
8. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 has also appeared and has filed an affidavit and in the affidavit, the said compromise has been acknowledged.
Learned counsel for the applicant has next submitted, on instructions, that opposite party No. 2 has no objection if the entire proceedings are quashed.

9. This Court is not unmindful of the judgements of the Apex Court in the cases of :-
1. B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another (2003) 4 SCC 675.
2. Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation [2008) 9 SCC 677].
3. Manoj Sharma Vs. State and others ( 2008) 16 SCC 1.
4. Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303.
5. Narindra Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab ( 2014) 6 SCC 466.
Wherein the Apex Court has categorically held that compromise can be made between the parties even in respect of certain cognizable and non compoundable offences.

sentences.text: 2 10. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, as noted herein above, and also the submissions made by the counsel for the parties, the court is of the considered opinion that no useful purpose shall be served by prolonging the proceedings of the above mentioned case.

11. Accordingly, the entire proceedings of Case No. 39 of 2023 (State vs. Devesh Garg) arising out of Case Crime No. 15 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 427 IPC and 3/4 of D.P. Act, P.S. Mahila Thana, District- Mainpuri, pending in the court of Civil Judge (Senior Division)/FTC (CAW),
Mainpuri, are hereby quashed.
